label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
Hi Mikaela, sorry this took a few days, I wanted to do it properly. You helped us heaps when Dave did his shoulder so you get the real version, bad bits and all.

We started on 21 Sept, once mating was under way. 290 cows, mostly 3-way crosses. We skip the arvo milking on Tues, Thurs, Sat and Sunday, so four once-a-day days a week. Mornings are still 5.15 every day, that part doesn't change.

Production first. Milksolids are down about 6% on the same weeks last year, going off the Fonterra app. Our rep told us to expect 8 to 10, so we've come out better than he reckoned, but it's still 6% gone and you need to be ok with that before you start.

Cells, yes they jumped. We went from 110k to about 180k in the first 3 weeks. They've settled back to around 135k now, so not mental, but not back where they were either.

Now the bad one. We had a heifer with mastitis go bad on a skipped arvo. Nobody spotted it till the next morning and she lost a quarter. On twice a day we'd have picked her up that afternoon. So you have to be on your game with teat spraying, and someone has to actually go and look at the cows on the skip days. If you get slack on that it bites you, and it bit us.

The good stuff. Lame cows are way down, 4 on the list now against 11 this time last year. Our walk to the back paddocks is 1.8km and I put it down to them not doing that trip four afternoons a week. The cows also came round quicker than I thought. About 4 days of bellowing at the gate, then they were fine.

Then there's the people side, which is the bit that sold me. The first Sunday arvo we skipped, Dave and I drove to Hamilton to see the grandkids. First Sunday off in spring in 20 odd years. And Kieran, our 2IC, told me it's the first spring he hasn't wanted to quit by October. Might be worth knowing with your young fella talking about leaving.

Honestly I wouldn't go back. The hours alone are worth the 6% to us. But that's our farm and our cows, and I'm not going to promise it goes the same at yours. I don't want you cursing me in March! What I will say is if Tom's knees are stuffed, having those arvos off will help him more than anything else you could change.

I'll bring our shed rosters and the numbers to the field day on the 19th so you can have a proper look at how we've set it up. Grant, you're welcome to a look too if you're still keen.

Or just ring me, Mikaela. Much easier than texting and my thumbs are useless on this thing.
